# Edit Log — 2026-09-03

## v131.12 — 2026-09-03 — Change (changelog): translate displayed entry titles/scopes to Arabic

**Why:** The "سجل التحديثات" (Latest Updates) tab's headings and badge labels were already Arabic, but each entry's title/scope came straight from `LATEST_UPDATES` (auto-generated from `docs/edit logs/*.md`), which are written in English per this file's own convention — leaving the visible list mixed-language even though the rest of the page is RTL Arabic. Hand-editing the generated data file wasn't viable (`npm run generate:changelog` overwrites it), and requiring bilingual edit-log entries going forward was out of scope for this change.

**What changed:** Added `src/data/changelog/titleTranslations.ts`, a version-keyed lookup (`TITLE_TRANSLATIONS`) and scope-slug lookup (`SCOPE_TRANSLATIONS`) providing Arabic display text for the entries currently in `LATEST_UPDATES`; entries with no mapping fall back to their raw English text so nothing silently disappears. `Changelog/index.tsx` now renders `translateTitle(entry.version, entry.title)` and `translateScope(entry.scope)` instead of the raw fields. The edit-log source files and the generator script are untouched — only the on-screen text changes.

**File:** `dist/index.html`

**File:** `package.json`

**File:** `src/components/Sidebar/Tabs/Changelog/index.tsx`

**File:** `src/data/changelog/titleTranslations.ts (new)`

**Before:**
```tsx
<p className="chg-title">
  {entry.scope && <span className="chg-scope">({entry.scope})</span>} {entry.title}
</p>
```

**After:**
```tsx

const title = translateTitle(entry.version, entry.title);
// ...

  {scope && <span className="chg-scope">({scope})</span>} {title}
</p>
```

## v131.11 — 2026-09-03 — Change (performance): replace unreadable team-mode working-hours rows with a monthly gaps bar chart

**Why:** The "ساعات العمل اليومية" chart's team view (no employee selected) rendered one row per employee per day, with a time-of-day gap track and text chips underneath each row. As a month accumulated days this became a long, unreadable wall of rows — reported directly by the user.

**What changed:** In team mode, the chart now renders a single stacked bar chart, one bar per calendar month, split by gap tier (small/medium/large; "normal"/"unclassified" excluded, same convention as before). A new `aggregateGapsByMonth()` in `performanceMetrics.ts` groups gaps by `YYYY-MM` and sums duration per tier; a new `gapsByMonthSvg()` in `performanceCharts.ts` renders it, following the existing `samplesTrendSvg` bar-chart pattern (RTL month order, no raw hex literals, `esc()`-routed labels). A `formatMonthLabel()` helper was added to `userManagementFormatters.ts` for the Arabic month/year axis labels. The detailed per-gap log (employee/day/start/end/duration/tier) already exists as a table below the charts (`سجل الفجوات` / `um-perf-gaps`), so nothing was duplicated there — the old inline per-row chips were simply dropped from the chart itself. Per-employee mode (an employee selected) is unchanged: it still shows one row per day, which stays readable since it's scoped to a single person.

## v131.10 — 2026-09-03 — Fix (distribution): guarantee a port-trapped employee's only reachable capacity instead of splitting it by raw need

**Why:** v131.9 (this same file, above) fixed each port re-apportioning independently by raw percentage, but weighting each port purely by an employee's *remaining stage-wide need* still had a gap: an employee eligible for only one small port, alongside colleagues who could also reach a much bigger port, had that small port split "fairly" by need even though the colleagues had 900 other rows to fall back on and the trapped employee had nowhere else to go. Verified counterexample (4 employees at 25% each of 1000 rows; a 900-row port reachable by a/b/c, a 100-row port reachable only by a/d): the v131.9 algorithm gave `a=307, b=322, c=321, d=50` — d stuck at 20% of target — when `300/300/300/100` was achievable and fair given d's actual reachable capacity.

**What changed:** Before apportioning each port, `calculateBulkAssignment` now splits each eligible employee's remaining need into a "forced" portion (need that exceeds their capacity across all NOT-YET-VISITED ports — i.e. this port is their last chance at some or all of it) and an "elastic" portion (the rest). Forced amounts are guaranteed outright (or, if forced demand exceeds the port's row count, scaled down proportionally to forced urgency); only the leftover rows are apportioned by elastic need. This stops the port an employee is trapped in from being shared "equally" with colleagues who have plenty of alternative capacity elsewhere. Also extracted the percentage→Hamilton-weight conversion (previously duplicated in two places) into a shared `allocWeight` helper.

**File:** `dist/index.html`

**File:** `src/data/changelog/latestUpdates.generated.ts`

**File:** `src/data/distribution/bulkAssignment.test.ts`

**File:** `src/data/distribution/bulkAssignment.ts`

**Before:**
```ts
const portAllocs: EmployeeStageAllocation[] = eligibleAllocs.map((a) => ({
  ...a,
  method: "exact",
  value: remainingNeed.get(a.username) ?? 0, // weighted purely by remaining need
}));
```

**After:**
```ts
const laterPorts = portGroups.slice(i + 1);
const forced = new Map<string, number>();
for (const alloc of eligibleAllocs) {
  const need = remainingNeed.get(alloc.username) ?? 0;
  const otherCapacity = laterPorts.reduce(
    (sum, later) => sum + (isPortEligible(alloc.username, later.portKey, portRestrictions) ? later.portRows.length : 0),
    0
  );
  forced.set(alloc.username, Math.max(0, need - otherCapacity));
}
const totalForced = [...forced.values()].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);

let portAllocs: EmployeeStageAllocation[];
if (totalForced >= portRows.length) {
  portAllocs = eligibleAllocs.map((a) => ({ ...a, method: "exact", value: forced.get(a.username) ?? 0 }));
} else {
  const elasticRows = portRows.length - totalForced;
  const elasticAlloc = hamiltonApportionment(
    eligibleAllocs.map((a) => ({
      key: a.username,
      size: Math.max(0, (remainingNeed.get(a.username) ?? 0) - (forced.get(a.username) ?? 0)),
    })),
    elasticRows
  );
  const elasticMap = new Map(elasticAlloc.map((q) => [q.key, q.allocated]));
  portAllocs = eligibleAllocs.map((a) => ({
    ...a,
    method: "exact",
    value: (forced.get(a.username) ?? 0) + (elasticMap.get(a.username) ?? 0),
  }));
}
```

**Verification:**
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run test:run` — 457 files / 4333 tests passed, including two new regression tests: one reproducing the trapped-employee counterexample above (asserts the ideal `300/300/300/100` split, which the v131.9 algorithm could not produce) and one confirming unequal configured percentages (20%/80%) are still respected exactly under restrictions, not defaulted to an equal split
- `npm run build` — succeeds, `dist/index.html` regenerated

## v131.9 — 2026-09-03 — Fix (distribution): keep per-employee sample totals equal when port restrictions are active

**Why:** With any employee port-restricted, `calculateBulkAssignment` partitioned a stage's rows by port and re-apportioned each port independently at 100% among only that port's eligible employees, using each employee's raw configured percentage as the weight. A restricted employee's excluded share on the ports they couldn't reach was never made up elsewhere, and employees who happened to share fewer ports with others were over-weighted on those ports — so with four employees configured at an equal 25% each, real totals drifted to reports like 1,800 / 2,000 / 2,500 / 1,400 instead of an equal split.

**What changed:** Before partitioning a restricted stage by port, `calculateBulkAssignment` now computes each employee's overall target for the WHOLE stage once (Hamilton apportionment of the stage's total row count by their configured percentage/exact value), then processes ports most-constrained-first (fewest eligible employees first) and apportions each port using each eligible employee's *remaining* stage-wide need as an exact-count weight, decrementing that shared pool as rows are actually assigned. This keeps every employee's final total anchored to their configured percentage regardless of how the stage happens to split across ports, while an employee with fewer allowed ports still draws a bigger share of the ports they can reach to make up the difference.

**File:** `dist/index.html`

**File:** `src/data/distribution/bulkAssignment.test.ts`

**File:** `src/data/distribution/bulkAssignment.ts`

**Before:**
```ts
for (const [portKey, portRows] of rowsByPort) {
  const eligibleAllocs = stageAllocs.filter((a) => isPortEligible(a.username, portKey, portRestrictions));
  if (eligibleAllocs.length === 0) {
    errors.push(/* ... */);
    continue;
  }

  const group = assignWithinGroup({
    rows: portRows,
    stageAllocs: eligibleAllocs, // raw percentage weights, renormalized to 100% per port
    assignableEmployees,
    contextLabel: `${stageKey} - ${portKey}`,
    operatorUsername,
    month,
    year,
  });
  events.push(...group.events);
  errors.push(...group.errors);
}
```

**After:**
```ts
const remainingNeed = new Map(
  hamiltonApportionment(
    stageAllocs.map((a) => ({
      key: a.username,
      size: Math.max(0, a.method === "percentage" ? Math.round(a.value * 100) : a.value),
    })),
    stageRows.length
  ).map((q) => [q.key, q.allocated])
);

const portGroups = [...rowsByPort.entries()]
  .map(([portKey, portRows]) => ({
    portKey,
    portRows,
    eligibleAllocs: stageAllocs.filter((a) => isPortEligible(a.username, portKey, portRestrictions)),
  }))
  .sort((a, b) =>
    a.eligibleAllocs.length !== b.eligibleAllocs.length
      ? a.eligibleAllocs.length - b.eligibleAllocs.length
      : a.portKey < b.portKey ? -1 : a.portKey > b.portKey ? 1 : 0
  );

for (const { portKey, portRows, eligibleAllocs } of portGroups) {
  if (eligibleAllocs.length === 0) {
    errors.push(/* ... */);
    continue;
  }

  const portAllocs = eligibleAllocs.map((a) => ({
    ...a,
    method: "exact" as const,
    value: remainingNeed.get(a.username) ?? 0, // shared remaining need, not raw percentage
  }));

  const group = assignWithinGroup({ rows: portRows, stageAllocs: portAllocs, /* ... */ });
  events.push(...group.events);
  errors.push(...group.errors);

  for (const event of group.events) {
    remainingNeed.set(event.assignedTo, Math.max(0, (remainingNeed.get(event.assignedTo) ?? 0) - 1));
  }
}
```

**Verification:**
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run test:run` — 457 files / 4331 tests passed, including a new regression test (`calculateBulkAssignment keeps every employee's total near their equal percentage even when one is port-restricted`) that fails against the pre-fix algorithm (one employee lands at 284/1000 instead of ~250) and passes with the fix
- `npm run build` — succeeds, `dist/index.html` regenerated
